messages:
aria: Quick sync — planning to roll out the new routing-weights-at-scale flag. Question: if project-level enable=true, and a route sets disable=true, which wins? I thought precedence was route > model > project > org?
sam: For the current implementation: route > model > project > org, yes. BUT org-level flags with tag:guardrail are treated as mandatory — they can only be set to soft_allow at lower scopes, not hard_override.
leo: Fwiw we added an explicit check in the resolver to avoid silent org violations. If a lower-scope enables something that conflicts with an org guardrail, the request is rejected and logged to audits.
aria: Ah ok. So a route cannot flip an org guardrail off. Good. Any nuance with model-level defaults when a route specifies audience-based canaries?
mika: Model-level flags are defaults for all routes using that model. If route defines a canary audience, we evaluate audience filters first (to decide whether the flag applies), then apply scope precedence for the matched bucket. Example: route A targets 10% users to model-override, those users get model-level value if route doesn't explicitly set it.
sam: Example config we've been using in tests: ```json
{
  "org": { "routing-debug": "off", "guardrail": ["routing-debug"] },
  "project": { "routing-debug": "on" },
  "models": {
    "m-v2": { "routing-debug": "on" }
  },
  "routes": {
    "route-ux": { "routing-debug": "off", "canary": { "pct": 10, "audience": "beta-users" } }
  }
}
```
leo: In that payload route-ux users in beta-users -> route setting off wins. Non-beta users -> model/project wins (depending on presence). Org guardrail would still block if it lists "routing-debug" as forbidden.
aria: Got it. One more: if a rollout uses "soft_enable" at project scope and route sets hard_enable for a canary, do we allow it? I remember a debate on soft vs hard.
mika: We treat soft_enable as advisory — metrics/quality check required before automated promotion. But hard_enable from a lower scope can be allowed only if there's an explicit opt-in in the project config (project.allow_hard_from_lower=true). Otherwise resolver downgrades to soft_enable and emits a warning.
sam: TL;DR: Precedence still route>model>project>org, but guardrails and explicit opt-out gates can alter behavior. Also watch out for the "allow_hard_from_lower" flag.
aria: Thanks. I'll update the rollout checklist and add a note about org guardrails + the allow_hard_from_lower gate.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for rollout/route-ux-canary — grouping by model m-v2 — ETA 20m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
aria: pinging @sam @mika if anything else to add before I merge the canary PR (#4721).
sam: lgtm, add a short blurb in the PR about guardrail behavior and I'll approve.
mika: approving once the tests for audience filter edge-cases pass (especially anon users).
aria: perfect — merging after tests. Thanks all :thumbsup:
